newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Polkomtel cellular firm plans loan by end97.
newsitem.headline: Polish Polkomtel cellular firm plans loan by end97.

text.p: Poland's digital cellular phone operator, Polkomtel SA, signed an agreement on Wednesday for a $221 million loan with a consortium of Polish banks and plans to seek another loan of double its size by the end of the year.

Polkomtel's finance director Poul Horup Sorensen told Reuters after the firm signed an agreement on a 10-month loan with seven Polish banks led by Bank Handlowy SA that the new borrowing would likely be for 7.5-8.5 years.
The loan would be used to pay back the initial $221 million loan and for further investments.

"We are preparing information packages to be sent out to the banks that could bid for that (the loan)...the loan would be longer and bigger, possibly twice as big as that one we signed today," he said.
He added foreign banks were likely to grant the new loan, but declined to give further details.
Under the Wednesday's agreement the consortium would lend Polkomtel at least 80 percent of the $221 million in zlotys with the rest extended in dollars or marks.
The banking consortium includes Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA, IBP Bank SA, PKO BP, Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA, Pekao SA and Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA.
Sorensen declined to give conditions of the loan due on December 15 and said the funds would be used for the expansion of Polkomtel's network.

Polkomtel, an international consortium which groups Danish Tele Danmark, U.S. AirTouch Communications, Polish copper concern KGHM SA, the Plock oil refinery and the National Power Grid (PSE) is one of Poland's two GSM system operators and markets its products under the Plus GSM brand.
